title: Don't Prompt Your Agents. Equip Them: Skillware as a Modular Standard for Sovereign, Auditable, and Deterministic Capability Execution for Logical Systems
title_zh: 不要提示你的智能体，要装备它们：Skillware作为逻辑系统实现主权、可审计且确定性能力执行的模块化标准

paragraphs.en: Skillware为智能体提供模块化确定性能力包，使小型本地模型在多步工作流上超越前沿模型并大幅降低成本。 Current autonomous logical systems rely on a fragile assumption: that language models should dynamically write code, guess API payloads, and memorize operational constraints through prompt engineering. In practice, this burns massive context windows, inflates API bills, and produces brittle agents that fail unpredictably in production. In this work, we present Skillware, an open architectural framework and capability registry that formally separates what an agent wants to do from how that task is executed. Instead of prompting models with loose text instructions or markdown files baptized as 'skills', Skillware equips them with modular, versioned software capability bundles. Much like skill hotkeys in video games that execute deterministically under fixed world rules, each bundle combines a typed JSON input contract, deterministic Python code, task directives, bundled datasets, and automated unit tests. In-process adapters translate these capabilities into native tool declarations for any model, from frontier cloud APIs to local open-weight runtimes with zero network latency. Evaluating 23 frontier and open-weight models across 368 benchmark conditions, we show that small local models (3B to 8B parameters) equipped with Skillware consistently outperform unequipped frontier models on complex multi-step workflows. They cut token usage by up to 84.8%, slash inference costs by up to 97.3%, and eliminate parameter errors entirely. True agent reliability does not come from larger models or longer prompts, but from equipping logical systems with verified, deterministic software. Finally, we articulate the trajectory of capability bundles across an invariant continuum of information processing systems: from digital logical systems today, to IoT, drones, and embodied robotics tomorrow, establishing a foundation for auditable, real-time capability execution.
paragraphs.zh: Skillware为智能体提供模块化确定性能力包，使小型本地模型在多步工作流上超越前沿模型并大幅降低成本。当前的自主逻辑系统依赖于一个脆弱的假设：语言模型应当动态编写代码、猜测API载荷，并通过提示工程记忆操作约束。 在实践中，这会消耗大量上下文窗口、推高API账单，并产生脆弱的智能体，在生产环境中以不可预测的方式失败。 在本工作中，我们提出Skillware，一个开放的架构框架与能力注册表，它从形式上将智能体想做什么与任务如何执行分离开来。 Skillware不是用松散的文本指令或被冠以「技能」之名的markdown文件来提示模型，而是为模型配备模块化、带版本的软件能力包。 就像电子游戏中在固定世界规则下确定性执行的技能快捷键一样，每个能力包将带类型的JSON输入契约、确定性Python代码、任务指令、内置数据集和自动化单元测试组合在一起。 进程内适配器将这些能力转换为任意模型的原生工具声明，从前沿云端API到零网络延迟的本地开放权重运行时均可支持。 通过在368个基准条件下评估23个前沿与开放权重模型，我们表明配备Skillware的小型本地模型（3B至8B参数）在复杂多步工作流上始终优于未配备的前沿模型。 它们将令牌使用量削减最高84.8%，将推理成本降低最高97.3%，并完全消除参数错误。 真正的智能体可靠性并非来自更大的模型或更长的提示，而是来自为逻辑系统配备经过验证的确定性软件。 最后，我们阐述了能力包在信息处理系统不变连续体上的发展轨迹：从今天的数字逻辑系统，到未来的物联网、无人机和具身机器人，为可审计的实时能力执行奠定基础。
